provenance.labels: pre-parse engineering expectations and stated review obligations; not observed parser outcomes or human preference judgments
provenance.reused_probe: reused_reads_ccomp preserves the exact earlier semicolon source and its declared period counterpart

scope.counting: Each pair contributes once to undirected eligibility; directional checks remain separate.

execution.rule_policy: Use unchanged split_independent_semicolon and join_independent_sentences; do not change preconditions after parsing.
execution.patch_policy: Exact grammar_core::edits::Edit byte offsets. Join has punctuation and first-subject capitalization patches, including declared no-op capitalization; split has one separator-through-first-subject-token patch.
execution.inverse_policy: Each exact declared candidate is the inverse case's source, and applying that inverse case's edits must restore the original bytes.
execution.expectation_policy: Compare bool expected_rule_candidate with exact candidate emission; null is an explicitly exploratory parser-dependent probe and must not be counted as an expectation pass.
execution.guard_policy: No guard-pass labels are asserted. Run the unchanged guard separately and retain observed_preserved, changed, unresolved, unavailable correspondence and all findings.
execution.guard_candidate_cap: The existing guard internally uses rules::MAX_CANDIDATES=256 for rule matching; this frozen limitation remains explicit.
execution.selection_policy: No preference scoring, threshold selection, corpus allocation, automatic edit adoption or model fitting in this fixture.
execution.layout_policy: Preserve the declared separators and casing exactly; do not repair quotation, paragraph or parser failures.

shared_review_obligations: Preserve every actor, predicate, argument and qualification attached to its source claim.
Changes in punctuation and sentence-initial casing can change emphasis, rhythm and discourse interpretation; these require review.
A rule proposal or guard result is not a semantic-equivalence, readability, tonal-intent or detector certificate.
